queue.what: root-caused and fixed the fault reported at kernels/indexer.cu:91. Finding 53: k_topk_offset (and three sibling top-k scan kernels) requested exactly n*sizeof(float) of dynamic shared memory while nvcc widens the scan into a 12-byte vectorised load, so any n<3 reads out of bounds and the launch is killed. Fixed via topk_scan_smem() in include/indexer.h. Also fixed: gridDim-0 launches in compressor_forward (groups==0) and indexer_forward (T==0), and dsync() now drains + names the CUDA last-error slot, which the engine never read.
queue.falsify: one full-model run, NGEN0=60, with a prompt LONGER than 18 ids appended so SMAX>18, re-running cycle 3's gate points. Three outcomes at once: (a) does prompt 2 (s=18) now emit an identical sequence on repeated points, (b) does the indexer.cu fault recur, (c) does SMAX>18 change anything, which decides whether 'the prompt of length SMAX' was ever the right frame. Watch stderr for '[launch] file:line pending CUDA error'.
queue.note: the crashing prompt's T was 4, which does NOT over-read; two of the four prompts in that run (T=1 and T=2) did. So the fix is real and on the reported line but its sufficiency for the cycle-3 fault is UNPROVEN. Do not write it up as solved before the run.
